notes: Three verbless clauses take supplied verbs by what is left to carry them: the two relative clauses put are on the preposition under rule 53, headed on the prepositional word, and the opening clause, which expresses no subject at all, puts there is on the predicate noun θεός under rule 68, discontinuously across the numeral (rule 15).

Both τὰ πάντα phrases are analysed alike under rule 102, the article taking the supplied nominal things and the adjective taking all; reading all things as the adjective's whole realization under rule 17 with the article unrepresented remains defensible and the unit note records it.
Ἰησοῦς and Χριστός are split into separate units rather than sharing one head (rules 17, 28).
εἰς → unto carries no copula because the ASV supplies none in that clause; only the two relative clauses are completed.
